subject: Geography
central_question: Why does international trade develop, how is it organised, and what benefits and concerns arise from the exchange of goods and services across national boundaries?
in_scope_units: Meaning of trade, barter, money and international exchange.
Historical development of international trade from local exchange to global commerce.
Reasons and bases for international trade.
Balance of trade and its favourable or unfavourable condition.
Free trade, trade liberalisation and dumping.
World Trade Organisation and debates about global trade rules.
Regional trade blocs and concerns related to international trade.
Ports as gateways of trade and their classification.
banned_topics: Detailed global transport routes and communication technologies.
Detailed retail, wholesale and service-sector organisation.

known_pitfalls.claim: International trade is simply the movement of goods between places within one country.
known_pitfalls.correction: International trade is the exchange of goods and services among countries across national boundaries.

known_pitfalls.claim: A negative balance of trade means a country exports more than it imports.
known_pitfalls.correction: It is unfavourable when the value of imports exceeds the value of exports.

known_pitfalls.claim: Free trade automatically benefits every producer equally.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter warns that unequal conditions and dumping can harm developing economies and domestic producers.
